proof_summary: A finite divisibility check shows that for every \(1\le d\le2025\), one of the prime pairs \((11,13),(7,19),(5,29),(7,13),(7,11),(3,47),(2,73)\) has neither prime dividing \(d\). Since each pair has product at most \(150\) and distinct final digits, \(d\) is invertible modulo that product, so some index \(0\le i<150\) makes \(a+id\) divisible by both primes, contradicting the required common final digit of all prime divisors.
